children: US heating oil prices held around $5.20 per gallon, remaining near their record high and leaving them about 120% higher than a year earlier amid concerns over tightening distillate markets.

EIA data showed distillate inventories, including diesel and heating oil, rose by 1.6 million barrels in the week ended September 11, but remained 13% below their five-year average, underscoring continued inventory tightness.
This comes amid disruptions on multiple fronts, with Middle East supply constraints compounded by Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries and Russia’s export curbs.
Some pressure eased after Saudi Arabia offered additional crude through Oman.

Meanwhile, with the US harvest season underway and the winter heating season approaching, distillate demand could strengthen further, while seasonal refinery maintenance could constrain production and add pressure to already-tight supplies.

title: Heating Oil Holds Near Record High
